summary: The current arXiv batch is strongest on model-to-observable links: neural surrogates expose centrality-definition biases in heavy-ion simulations; a transport-plus-hydrodynamics calculation proposes jet-associated hadrochemistry as a medium-response observable; and nCTEQ26 supplies a substantial new nuclear-PDF baseline. On the AI/ML side, the most transferable results are a physics-controlled centrality surrogate, a data-driven CMS fake-background method, and a rate-distortion study of HEP tokenization. Evidence remains limited for deployment claims that rely only on particle-level or simulated-detector benchmarks.
strongest_paper_summary: A small hybrid-event sample is used to emulate final-state centrality observables at 1--2% relative error while explicitly quantifying the physics impact of centrality rebinning.

papers.title: Levy-shaped femtoscopic sources from an exact solution of relativistic hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: The paper presents an exact relativistic-hydrodynamic solution intended to produce Levy-shaped emission sources, addressing the tension between Levy fits to QGP femtoscopy and the Gaussian profiles often expected from hydrodynamics. It analyzes whether the solution is compatible with observations.

papers.title: Final-state centrality in relativistic heavy-ion simulations from neural networks
papers.abstract: Neural networks trained on a few hundred hybrid events predict event-by-event charged-particle multiplicity and mean transverse momentum with 1--2% relative errors. For Pb-Pb at 2.76 TeV and Au-Au at 200 GeV, the study quantifies how initial- and final-state centrality definitions differ, including up to 20% event reassignment in 1%-wide classes, and applies the result to fluctuation and correlation observables.

papers.title: Dijet hadrochemistry: tomography of jet-induced medium excitation and diffusion wake
papers.short_authors: Cong Yi, Xiang-Yu Wu, Zhong Yang, Pi Duan, Guang-You Qin, Xin-Nian Wang, Wenbin Zhao
papers.abstract: A coupled linear-Boltzmann-transport plus hydrodynamics calculation with hybrid hadronization predicts enhanced K/pi and p/pi ratios around jets in central Pb-Pb, especially near the subleading jet. The model also predicts a depletion near Delta phi approximately pi/2 whose hadrochemistry retains the signature of jet-excited medium, interpreted as a diffusion wake.

papers.title: nCTEQ26 nuclear parton distribution functions
papers.short_authors: nCTEQ Collaboration, K. Greve, T. Jezo, A. Kusina, J. Wissmann, M. Klasen, et al.
papers.abstract: The nCTEQ26 global analysis combines DIS, fixed-target Drell-Yan, RHIC and LHC data, including open-heavy-quark and quarkonium information, with a more flexible nuclear parametrization and target-mass and deuteron corrections. It provides Hessian uncertainties, comparisons to other analyses, predictions for future measurements, and public grids through LHAPDF and HEPForge.

papers.title: Probing high-momentum components in 16O via zero-degree (p,d) cross-section ratios
papers.short_authors: Super-FRS Experiment Collaboration, X. Wang, H. J. Ong, S. Terashima, I. Tanihata, Y. K. Tanaka, et al.
papers.abstract: Zero-degree 16O(p,d)15O measurements at proton energies of 403--1209 MeV extend earlier cross-section-ratio results and add the first ratio for the 7.28-MeV 7/2+ state. The positive-parity ratios show pronounced momentum dependence consistent with representative variational Monte Carlo trends, providing an experimental handle on high-momentum neutron components.

papers.title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays
papers.abstract: The MUFFIN method uses boosted-decision-tree reweighting to learn multidimensional per-object correction factors directly from observed 13.6 TeV CMS data. Relative to low-dimensional fake-factor parametrizations, it improves key kinematic distributions, especially at high transverse momentum, and the abstract reports reductions of up to 70% in the associated systematic uncertainty.

papers.title: Precision Tokenization for Multi-Modal Data in High Energy Physics
papers.short_authors: Jeffrey Krupa, Samuel Klein, Nilotpal Kakati, Daniel Murnane, Baran Hashemi, Eilam Gross, Lukas Heinrich, Michael Kagan
papers.abstract: The paper treats detector-data tokenization as a rate-distortion problem across four modalities and two simulated detectors. A systematic scan yields design rules; compression factors of about 4--11x retain performance for jet-pT regression, particle-flow reconstruction, and flavor tagging, with jet-pT resolution below 1%, and the authors release the heptokens library.

cautions.title: A Density Functional for Quark Matter with Screened Confinement Interactions
cautions.abstract: The paper constructs a quark-matter density functional from a screened linear confinement interaction and derives an interaction energy density proportional to n^(2/3).
